_meta.role: Robotics AI Engineer – Field Foundation Models & Dynamics Foundation Models

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built ROS2-based planning and control pipelines for robotic arms, deriving forward kinematics and executing collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on a physical UR5e, and developed CUDA-accelerated perception (TensorRT YOLO, 5.2x speedup) for a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic arm achieving 100% pick reliability across 10 trials. Additional background spans embedded C++/Python systems integration, sensor fusion, and adaptive path planning for autonomous vehicles, with hands-on comfort across the full field-deployment stack from algorithm design to hardware bring-up.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (AL5B & UR5e)
bullets: Derived DH tables and hand-computed full forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt and RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Planned and executed collision-free pick-and-place trajectories on physical UR5e via UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured at <2mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system over a three-layer distributed pipeline: Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino controller over a unified WebSocket fabric.
Integrated faster-whisper STT, TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2x speedup, 17.6→92 FPS) for visual servoing, and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors for contact-aware grasping via I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures; achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

projects.name: Autonomous Driving in CARLA
bullets: Built automated data generation pipelines using CARLA's semantic segmentation and raycast occlusion filtering to produce ~5,000 YOLO and ~3,000 UFLD training frames with zero manual annotation.
Trained YOLO11n (mAP50~0.85) and fine-tuned UFLD (ResNet-18) into an adaptive control stack with lane-following and waypoint fallback; validated with zero collisions across multiple laps.

awards: Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
